decisions.thought:
Lead: 34% BRING: dragapult, 27% BRING: aegislash, 25% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 2: 53% BRING: gholdengo, 21% BRING: aegislash, 10% BRING: corviknight
Pick 3: 37% BRING: aegislash, 27% BRING: kingambit, 20% BRING: corviknight

The opponent is heavy on Steel types, which Garchomp's Earthquake and Incineroar's Flare Blitz pressure well. Incineroar's Intimidate and Fake Out add control. Gholdengo covers the Dragapult and Ghost-weak matchups with Shadow Ball.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm looking at team preview against a steel-heavy opponent lineup with aegislash, corviknight, gholdengo, kingambit, and archaludon, so I'm weighing which of my six—incineroar, garchomp, gholdengo, kingambit, sinistcha, archaludon—gives the best coverage against that much steel, favoring fire, ground, or fighting options to pick three.

Garchomp's Earthquake hammers nearly every steel on their team except flying-immune corviknight, and Incineroar's fire plus intimidate/fake out/parting shot also pressures them well; I'm also considering Dragapult as a dragon/ghost threat that Gholdengo's ghost-type moves could handle better than Sinistcha's grass typing would.

I'm settling on incineroar, garchomp, and gholdengo for a solid mix of intimidate support, ground coverage, and ghost/steel offense.

decisions.thought: 40% MOVE: shadowball, 22% SWITCH: aegislash, 16% SWITCH: gholdengo
Dragapult outspeeds Incineroar (142 vs 80), so it would hit first. Fake Out on this turn prevents Dragapult's attack via flinch and chips it, which is the standard lead play here.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since Incineroar just entered this turn, Fake Out is available and will flinch Dragapult since it's not Normal-type immune, preventing Dragapult's faster attack and landing some chip damage before considering a follow-up Flare Blitz.

decisions.thought: 44% MOVE: shadowball, 29% SWITCH: aegislash, 27% SWITCH: gholdengo

Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragapult's Dragon typing, so Incineroar's attack is weak here. Parting Shot cuts Dragapult's Attack and Special Attack, and Incineroar switches out to bring in Garchomp, whose Outrage hits Dragapult for super-effective damage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's at 169/202 against Dragapult at full health, but my Atk is already down from Intimidate. Flare Blitz won't be effective since Dragapult resists Fire through its Dragon typing. Dark-type moves would hit harder given Dragapult's Ghost typing, though Parting Shot could also be useful to cut Dragapult's offensive stats and pivot out.

Switching to Garchomp looks promising since Dragon is super effective against Dragapult's own Dragon typing, and Earthquake would land neutral damage too. Gholdengo is another consideration, but I'm second-guessing whether its Steel/Ghost typing actually helps against Dragapult's Shadow Ball -- Steel doesn't resist Ghost, so Gholdengo would take that hit at full effectiveness rather than resisting it.

Actually, Steel does resist Dragon, so Dragapult's Dragon-type attacks would be weakened against Gholdengo. Given this, I think Incineroar's best play here is Parting Shot -- it drops Dragapult's Attack and Special Attack while letting me pivot to Garchomp or Gholdengo next turn with better matchup odds, even though Garchomp is slower and would take an Outrage hit first.

Incineroar got forced out after Parting Shot, so now I need to pick between Garchomp and Gholdengo to replace it. I'm weighing matchups against Dragapult, which is Dragon/Ghost, so Garchomp's Dragon typing could be risky if it eats a dragon-type move.

Gholdengo's weak to Fire, Ground, Dark, Ghost, so Shadow Ball lands super effective on it too, and with 164 HP and only -1 SpA it still hits hard with Life Orb. I'm now comparing speeds—Dragapult's base 142 and Garchomp's 102 versus Gholdengo's 84, trying to figure out who actually moves first here.

Comparing STAB multipliers: Garchomp's Outrage gets double Dragon STAB against Dragapult's Dragon/Ghost typing, while Gholdengo's Shadow Ball similarly gets doubled Ghost STAB against that same typing, so both attacks hit for massive damage against Dragapult.

Running the raw numbers, Outrage against Dragapult's defense comes out ahead of Shadow Ball against its special defense, so Garchomp hits harder despite speed concerns about who moves first—I'll go with Garchomp for the stronger damage output.
